messages.author: 3bcefa1ca39a6742
messages.subject: Re: The Bank updates
parts:
Thanks very much for the Bank Tutorial Part I and Part II. I found it very useful. I was trying to create a variant of the bank example as follows:
1. There two sets of customers (customers1 whose tasks are longer to process, and customers2 whose tasks are shorter to process).
2. There are 2 resources (a) Counter 1 that gives priority to customers1 and services customers2 only when no customer1 is in the queue (b) Counter 2 that services only customers2.

I couldn't figure out how to impose the logic above on resources. I would appreciate any thoughts you might have. Below is an example code that I created when customers1/counter 1 and customers2/counter 2 are independent of each other and just a few customers. 

arrtime1 = 15
servicetime1 = 10

arrtime2 = 8
servicetime2 = 5

env = simmer()

cust1 = trajectory() %>%
        seize("counter1") %>%
        timeout(function() servicetime1) %>%
        release("counter1")

cust2 = trajectory() %>%
        seize("counter2") %>%
        timeout(function() servicetime2) %>%
        release("counter2")

env %>% add_resource("counter1", 1) %>%
        add_resource("counter2", 1) %>%
        add_generator("cust1", cust1, at(0)) %>%
        add_generator("cust2", cust2, at(0, 3)) %>%
        run(until = 100)

Thanks,
Shankar

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: The Bank updates
parts:
You need to implement a sort of token bucket for customer2 using an
additional resource:

library(simmer)

servicetime1 <- 5
servicetime2 <- 10

customer1 <- trajectory() %>%
set_capacity("token", 1) %>%

seize("counter1") %>%
timeout(function() servicetime1) %>%

release("counter1") %>%
set_capacity("token", function() {
if (get_queue_count(env, "counter1"))
1
else 2
})

customer2 <- trajectory() %>%
seize("token") %>%
select(paste0("counter", 1:2), "first-available") %>%
seize_selected() %>%
timeout(function() {
if (get_selected(env) == "counter1")
servicetime1
else servicetime2
}) %>%
release_selected() %>%
release("token")

env <- simmer()
env %>%
add_resource("token", 2) %>%
add_resource("counter1") %>%
add_resource("counter2") %>%
add_generator("customer1", customer1, at(3, 8, 9)) %>%
add_generator("customer2", customer2, at(0, 1, 2)) %>%
run()

Note that this won't work if you run into simultaneous events in some
cases. If you use random distributions for arrival/service times, you
are safe.

Iñaki

Thanks very much for the suggestion on using tokens and the code below. This is a great idea and was very helpful. 

I also tried an alternate approach without tokens but using priority of 1 for customer 1. Below is example code and the output I got. Somehow this approach is not working (for example I was thinking customer 21 will select counter 2 but is selecting counter 1). I would appreciate if you can help me understand where my logic is wrong with the code below.

servicetime2 <- 5

env <- simmer()
customer1 <- trajectory() %>%
log_("Cust 1 in") %>%
seize("counter1") %>%
log_("started in counter1") %>%

timeout(function() servicetime1) %>%
    release("counter1") %>%
log_("released counter1")
customer2 <- trajectory() %>%
log_("cust 2 in") %>%
select(paste0("counter", 1:2), "first-available") %>%

log_(function() paste0("selected ", get_selected(env))) %>%

        if (get_selected(env) == "counter1")

        else servicetime2

log_("released resource")

env %>%

add_resource("counter1") %>%
    add_resource("counter2") %>%

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: The Bank updates
parts:
The problem with your approach is that there may be customer2 arrivals
sitting in the queue of counter2 and then counter1 becomes available.
You would need some mechanism to exit that queue and try counter1
again. This could be implemented using renege_if and signals, but I
think it's more complicated than my approach.

Iñaki

events, and this is because all your service and interarrival times
are integers. You can debug with simmer(verbose=TRUE) to see what's
happening, but this issue won't happen as soon as you start using
random distributions.
